Part 1 · The method

How does a HAZOP examine a design, one section at a time?

Part 1 · the plan

Intent, deviation, cause, consequence

  1. What a HAZOP isa team compares the design with its intent
  2. Four phasesdefinition, preparation, examination, follow-up
  3. Nodes and design intentwhere one node ends and the next begins
  4. Guide word × parameterhow deviations are generated
  5. One worksheet rowcause → consequence → safeguards → rank → action

1 · What a HAZOP is

A structured, team-based look at the P&ID

Design intent

What each section must do, with its numbers.

Deviation

A guide word applied to a parameter: NO flow, MORE temperature.

Two kinds of finding

Hazards (toxic gas, hot acid) and operability (cannot meet the permit).

Standard: IEC 61882:2016, application guide for HAZOP studies.

2 · Four phases

From scope to close-out

1Definitionscope from air and sulfur in to the stack; team; risk matrix
2PreparationP&ID, alarm list, trips, procedures; nodes and intents
3Examinationnode by node, guide word by guide word
4Follow-upworksheets, actions, close-out, revalidation

3 · Nodes and design intent

Node N4: what the boiler section must do

A node ends where the intent changes: a pump, a furnace, a boiler, a bed, an absorber.

Equipment
B-101, bypass TV-201, dilution air
Intent
cool furnace gas 1121 → 274 °C
Steam
94 t/h at 4.0 MPa g
Bed-1 inlet
420 °C, 12.0 % SO₂, 9.0 % O₂
Control
TIC-201 moves TV-201 (fails closed)

Every deviation in N4 is measured against these numbers.

4 · Guide word × parameter · click one of each

Generating the deviations

Many pairs give nothing meaningful — the team records only the deviations that are physically possible.

5 · One worksheet row

The columns of a HAZOP worksheet

Deviationguide word × parameter
→
Causeswhat makes it happen
→
Consequenceno credit for safeguards
→
Safeguardsalready designed in
→
S × Lrank with safeguards
→
Actionrecommendation

Severity S is judged without safeguards; likelihood L with them working.

Every meaningful deviation is written down, even when the safeguards are enough (full recording).

5 · Interactive · click Next to walk the row

Row N2.1: the blower stops

The consequence is written as if nothing worked — only then do the safeguards earn their place in the row.

5 · Who fills the row

The HAZOP team

Leader (chair)

Independent; runs the method.

Scribe

Writes the worksheet live.

Process engineer

Intent, balances, limits.

Operations

Start-up, upsets, rounds.

Instrument / control

Loops, fail positions, trips.

Safety / risk

Matrix, toxic consequences, LOPA.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • HAZOP compares each node of the P&ID with its design intent (IEC 61882).
  • Guide word × parameter gives the deviations; only meaningful ones are recorded.
  • A row runs deviation → causes → consequence → safeguards → S × L → action.
  • Severity ignores safeguards; likelihood credits them.

1 · The node map · click a node

The converter in ten nodes

Utilities and procedures are nodes too — one air failure moves every valve, and start-up creates deviations steady operation never sees.

2 · Worked row 1 of 3 · node N2

NO flow: the blower stops

The map gave the nodes. Now three of their highest rows, column by column.

Causes
K-101 motor trip; suction blocked
Consequence
sulfur vapour builds up in a hot furnace, ignites when air returns
Safeguards
I-1 FSLL-100 < 90 kNm³/h, 3 s; FI-100 LO 200; ESD
S × L
4 × 3 = 12 High
Action R08
second, diverse input to I-1

I-1 reads the same flow element as the FI-100 indication: one meter fault defeats both.

2 · Worked row 2 of 3 · node N8

NO flow: final-absorber acid stops

Causes
P-302A trips; P-302B is a manual spare
Consequence
SO₃ leaves the stack as a dense acid-mist plume
Safeguards
FI-302 LO 750 m³/h; I-4 FSLL-302 < 500 m³/h, 10 s
S × L
4 × 3 = 12 High
Action R24
auto-start for P-302B, like P-301B

2 · Worked row 3 of 3 · node N5

OTHER THAN measurement: TI-203 fails low

Causes
open-circuit thermocouple; wiring fault
Consequence
alarm and trip both blind to a real bed-1 over-temperature
Safeguards
TI-202 indication; stack SO₂ alarm, late
S × L
4 × 3 = 12 High
Action R20
trip on its own 2oo3 elements

2oo3: two out of three separate elements must agree to trip.

3 · All rows of a node · click a node

What each worksheet contains

Each node mixes hazards and operability — most rows are Medium; the few High ones drive the actions.

4 · Coverage

Which guide words did the work

MORE, LESS and NO give 64 of 94 rows; the time words act in the procedure node N10.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • Ten nodes: eight process, utilities N9, procedures N10.
  • 94 deviations recorded; every one of the 11 guide words was used.
  • Blower stop and loss of final-absorber acid rank High; their trips need diverse inputs or spares.
  • A shared element blinds the alarm and the trip at once.

1 · The 5 × 5 matrix · click a cell

Where the 94 deviations fall

Shared matrix of the HAZID and HAZOP tabs$R = S \times L$

Eight rows are High and none Very high — each High row carries an action and may go to LOPA.

2 · Safeguard credit · switch safeguards off and on

What a safeguard is worth

Only independent safeguards earn credit — an alarm seconds before the trip, or a rule on paper, is worth little.

3 · Dynamic check

Running deviations on the model

The matrix ranks by judgement. The simulator can test some of those judgements.

Copy of the modelat design, live plant untouched
→
Apply deviationfault or wrong mode
→
Safeguards activealarms, trips, fail positions
→
No operatorup to 30 min
→
Recordalarms each second; stop 2 min after a trip

Ten runs, D1–D10, in the HAZOP tab; five are traced on the next slide.

    3 · Dynamic check

    Three lessons the worksheets alone missed

    A trip stops sulfur, not heat

    709 °C TI-203 after TSHH-203 (D3) → R43

    A shared element blinds two layers

    792 °C TI-202, no TSHH-203 trip (D5) → R20

    A trip limits duration, not peak

    3548 mg/Nm³ mist as FSLL-302 trips (D8) → R24

    Part 3 · summary

    What Part 3 settled

    • 94 rows: 0 Very high, 8 High, 77 Medium, 9 Low.
    • Only independent safeguards earn likelihood credit.
    • Model runs exposed post-trip heating, a shared element and a late trip.
    • 43 actions go to owners, LOPA, MOC and the 81-page report.

    This deck

    Key Takeaways

    1

    State each node's design intent with numbers before applying guide words.

    2

    Write the consequence as if no safeguard worked.

    3

    Credit only safeguards that are independent and fast enough.

    4

    Test the key judgements on the model when one exists.

    5

    Close every action with an owner, a date and a signature.
